name: AbilityLifecycle
summary: The order in which the game reads an ability, from the skillset row that offers it to the presentation and the save: where it comes from for a unit, the menus and lists, choosing and targeting, the action request and turn order, resolving, passive abilities, presentation, and what is stored. Each step names the functions and the id width at that point (8, 9, 10 or 16 bits); the width differs between steps, which is why an id that fits one step is cut at the next.

members.text: Decodes a set row (low byte + flag bit, 9 bit ids; sets above 226 give 0). Eleven functions call it.
Builds the 24-entry list of a set and sorts ids into ranges (below 0x1A6, 0x1A6..0x1C5, 0x1C6..0x1E6, above); 17 functions call it.

Maps a job to its set and filters by tab (tab 0 keeps ids 1..421); two more copies of the filter sit in Skillset_BuildTabAbilityList and sub_140392620. List words carry flags 0x1000/0x2000/0x4000 above a 10-bit id.
Learning sets a bit per slot of the job's set (22 bits per class); the bit means Skillset_GetAbility(set, slot).
The Item command maps item ids 240..253 to abilities 368..381 (item + 0x80) through a 14-byte table.
The post-battle roll learns from a 512-id bitmap and skips ids above 0x1FF.
JP cost is the Ability name row's value at +64; the learn screen rows go through the name-row getter.

Usable-ability lists per command (with sub_14030DD8C and sub_14030EC48); ids outside 1..0x16F and 406..413 are listed with no cost entry; a skillset that is neither the unit's primary nor secondary counts every slot as learned.
Writes the selection message whose +6 word is the chosen ability; the command-list word is cut to 9 bits here in stock.
Name, description, icon, JP and order key come from the Ability name table by key with no range check on the id (24 calls in 18 functions).
Confirm handler: stores the shape result at unit +0x194 and cuts unit +0x17A to 9 bits before reading the aux row.
Marks range and area from the action record; returns -1 for ids at or above 368 (with BattleRange_MarkRing and BattleRange_MarkArea).
Checks and pays MP only for ids up to 0x16F with command kind 0; the preview twin is sub_14030B1A0.
Validates the candidate and writes the request block at unit +0x1A0 (ability word at +0x1A2, 10 bit id plus unit); an item request is rewritten by +0x80.
Cuts the packed word to id & 0x3FF and builds the current-action block; reads the kind 1, 3 and 4 tables; ids at or above 368 get no record.
Stores the ability low byte plus bit 0x80 in a 4-byte entry (9 bits, no spare bit); the two panel readers decode it.
Scans targets from the range marks and calls Battle_ResolveAction for each; writes the effect word and the 512 sentinel.
Takes the action row (id below 368, else row 0), clamps the formula byte at +8 to 1..106, calls the handler from the 106-entry registry, then runs the post tests for formula below 7 and equal to 100.
Handlers read the ability id from the formula block word at 0x1407B0778; five of them switch on it; one re-indexes the registry unclamped.
Innate and equipped reaction, support and movement ids 0x1A6..0x1FD become bits at unit +0x94..+0x9E.
The tail tests the bits in a fixed order and hands the first hit to a Brave-roll helper; the executor sub_1403095E4 handles 422..434, 438, 439, 444 and 446 only.
Animation, charge and text come from g_AbilityAnim (454 rows) indexed by the effect word, not by the ability id; 512 is a no-effect sentinel.
Effect_SelectForAbility (0x140319B50) maps ids below 454 to g_AbilityEffectNumber and 512..548 to a 37-row pseudo table.
Case 7 cuts the word to 9 bits, adds 0x7000 and stores it as a kind-6 entry; the resolver BattleMsg_ResolveEntry masks 0x7FF and reads the Ability name row.
Equipped reaction, support and movement ids are u16 in the save (A+8..13); learned abilities are bits per slot (ability_flag_00..21); skillset ids are bytes (A+7), u16 in the party record (B+96).

behavior.text: the id width differs per step: 9 bit at the aux accessor, the banner dispatcher, unit +0x17A and the turn entry; 10 bit in list words, the packed action word and unit +0x1A2; u16 in the save's equipped fields; 22 slot bits for learned state.
the ability kind is not stored; Ability_GetAuxRecord derives it from eight id thresholds and several list builders repeat the ranges.

the accessor caller sets match the research census: Ability_GetAuxRecord 18 functions, AbilityAction_GetRecord 33, Skillset_GetAbility 11, Skillset_BuildAbilityList 17, Ability_GetJpCost 7, JobAbilityList_Build 8 (IDA code references, 2026-11-10).

notes: Function names are the published reference names; the open database names some of them differently (same addresses).
open_questions: ? which 0x3FF masks act on an ability word (the notes disagree: 6 or 31 sites); ? what unit +0x17A holds.

name: ApplicationLifecycle
summary: The order from process entry to the first scene. The main thread runs the application loop and the Win32 message pump while the boot state machine starts the task threads. The game task thread resets and enters the outer loop, which clears and scans the save images, runs a scene, and either starts the title/opening path or takes the alternate transition loop. The message pump is the only normal exit; the game loop never returns.

members.text: The CRT calls WinMain. It reads argc and argv, builds the system and game listener blocks, and calls Game_Main with the system block.
The debugger gate, data directory, window/application creation and then the loop `while (App_RunFrame(...) && App_ProcessMessages(...))`.

Frame pacing and the update chain. The application frame chain drives the boot state machine; its state 2 calls the thread factory, which creates 17 task threads and installs Game_ThreadMain in task slot 0.
Drains up to ten Win32 messages per call. WM_QUIT ends the application loop, after which Game_Main tears the application down and WinMain returns to the CRT.
Runs on the game task thread: first-use 4 MB arena setup, 512x272 display state, the effect base reset, then the pre-loop reset and the outer loop.
The 15-byte wrapper calls Game_LoopReset, the reset body, and then Game_MainLoop.
Sets the 374x240 screen mode, clears the fade, battle and event state and the event counters, resets the scene/UI helpers and seeds the constant block.

Clears both save images, scans the save data, resets the scene task set, runs SceneLoop_Run and converts the returned code into the next step. It re-enters the scene phase after every transition and never returns.
Caller of Scene_Init. Runs one scene task per frame while scene flag bit 0 is set, then returns the hand-over code in dword_141876F94.
Resets the scene flags, page buffer and task stack. A non-zero mode calls TitleScene_Start; mode 0 clears the page index and calls OpeningScene_Start.

Mode 0 pushes opening task 0; task 0 starts the title scene when no movie is requested, and otherwise returns without changing the stack. A non-zero mode pushes the title task directly. The title task's exit writes the hand-over code that Game_MainLoop reads next.

Used when `dword_140D3A848` is 3 (not SceneLoop_Run's return code 3). It resets the scene inline, reads 0x8800 bytes of data kind 877 from sector 101, pushes task 9 (which moves to task 10, the fade/movie task) and runs the same per-frame dispatch without a hand-over code.

behavior.text: the message pump and the game loop are separate threads: WinMain, Game_Main, App_RunFrame and App_ProcessMessages run on the process's first thread, while the thread factory creates the 17 task threads with `beginthreadex` and stores Game_ThreadMain in task slot 0.

the boot state machine runs on the main thread before the game thread exists (rests on the factory creating the game thread during boot state 2 and on Game_Main's loop being the only frame loop at that point).
the slot-0 task thread is the one that reaches Game_MainLoop (rests on the task loop `sub_1402F3698` calling the entry stored in the slot).

the outer loop clears both save images before the first scan and again before the second scan; a completed scan enters the scene phase, and an error becomes a message panel that, once it closes, enters the scene phase.

the scene tasks write 0, 1, 2 or 3 into dword_141876F94; Game_MainLoop branches on those values (0 sets `byte_1407829FA` to 1 and clears `g_BattleModeFlag`, 2 clears event variable 85, 3 sets `xmmword_142FF9E14` to 1 and arms the countdown dword, 1 only clears `byte_1407829FA`).
the two title-menu starts (new game versus continue) are the likely owners of codes 0 and 1 (rests on the branch bodies and the title task's writes); the exact mapping is not decoded.
the alternate loop runs only when the battle/scene result dword_140D3A848 is 3; the other handled result codes skip it.
no path returns from Game_MainLoop. The process is ended from the message thread when WM_QUIT makes App_ProcessMessages return 0.
the menu-level meaning of the four hand-over codes and the timing of the countdown state in the outer loop.

notes: Earlier versions of this reference documented a fragment of Game_MainLoop (the entry fill and part of the save-scan state machine) as a separate function, Save_BootClear. The save/load menu is the `sub_140245C84` + `off_1408F9570` state machine inside Game_MainLoop; SceneLoop_RunAlt is the battle-result transition loop, not the save/load screen. The boot hand-over is described in text here so this flow does not depend on the boot flow record.
open_questions: ? the menu-level meaning of hand-over codes 0 and 1; ? the gameplay meaning of result codes 2, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 10; ? missing global records for dword_141876F94, dword_141876EE8, dword_142FF9EFC and dword_140D3A848.

name: AutoSaveRead
summary: How a resume entry reaches the game: the reader queues one request per entry name, a single read kick mounts the container, and the delivery function hands each entry to its object, where the header is validated and the body copied to the checkpoint or the battle buffer.

members.text: The reader asks for the main part of a point, then for the parts that point carries: all four for a rotating point 00..02, and the battle set's own parts for point 1.
Each part becomes a queued request: the object, the entry name and a flag go into a 328-byte record on the request vector.
One read kick for area `AUTOENHANCED` follows the requests; it mounts the container and reads every entry the queue names.
Each entry is handed to the delivery function: the 16-byte header goes into the object, the object's handler copies the payload, and the object's post-delivery step runs.
The object checks the stored CRC against the payload before it accepts the entry; a mismatch rejects it.
The import validates the payload header (tag, version 122, kind below 2, self-check product) and copies the summary bytes into the auto slot.
The materialiser copies the body: 40,164 bytes to the checkpoint for kind 0, or 668,112 bytes to the battle buffer with the control words and the inflated texture page for kind 1.
A battle-saved manual slot requests its own `resume_enmaNN_world.sav` through the same queue and kick, then unpacks the checkpoint.

behavior.text: requests are told apart by name (the `resume_` prefix), so a replacement that answers the read kick can serve exactly the resume entries and pass every other name to the game.
the kick is synchronous, so the entries are already in their objects when it returns.
the reader is reached from the title's Continue, from the load menu and from the battle-resume setup, so all three take the same path.
the delivered payload is the same shape the writer produced, so the reader needs no schema for the battle body.

notes: The header import and the materialiser run per part, so a battle resume pays for the 668,112-byte copy before the first turn and not when the file is mounted.
open_questions: ? the order in which the parts are materialised when several are requested at once.

name: AutoSaveWrite
summary: Where a resume entry comes from and when it is written: the per-frame flush turns dirty group buffers into named entries, stamps each with a CRC, and one write kick sends the whole container. The world-map save and a manual battle save reuse the same entry and the same kick.

members.text: Every frame the update calls the flush; it looks at four group buffers (main, world, attack, fturn) and does nothing when none is dirty.
World group dirty: queue `resume_enwm_main.sav`.
fturn group dirty: queue the battle set at point 1 through the same part fan-out; in both saved copies the set is main, world and attack, with no fturn entry.
main group dirty: queue all four parts at resume point ring[+0x30] + 2, then advance the ring modulo 3 (points 00..02).
Each name is formatted from the part table (main, world, attack, fturn) and the point; a per-group map deduplicates repeated names before anything is queued.
The queue function stamps the CRC over the payload and queues the entry with version 17, then marks the group clean.
One write kick for area `AUTOENHANCED` follows the flush when anything was queued; the container writer rebuilds the PNG from the queue.
A manual save made in battle queues its own `resume_enmaNN_world.sav` (NN = slot number) through the same entry function and the same write kick.
The world-map save calls the flush from a UI callback and kicks the same write; the `enwm_main` entry itself is queued by the per-frame flush's world branch, which runs a few frames earlier or later.

behavior.text: main is written last because the parts are queued in index order 1, 2, 3, 0.
the bodies are built before the flush (the battle handler and the pack code fill the group buffers); the flush only names, deduplicates and queues bytes.
world and main entries are kind 0, attack and fturn are kind 1, and the manual `enmaNN` entry is always kind 0 (it is the world buffer).
when no group is dirty nothing is queued, so the write kick is not issued every frame.

notes: The capture writes the two bodies elsewhere: the battle handler for kind 1 and the slot pack code for kind 0, which is why the flush can treat every group the same way.
open_questions: ? which scene event marks each of the three rotating resume points 00..02.

name: BattleMessageBanner
summary: How a message descriptor becomes text in the battle's centre banner: a battle handler calls the banner function, which resolves the descriptor to a message id and a template, fills the format arguments, sets the text node's expanded text, and the node is laid out and drawn. The last step is gated: a node whose gate is closed is still called but draws nothing.

members.text: A battle message handler calls the banner function (sub_140111D20): the two handlers at sub_1400E8930 / sub_1400E8A84 do so after the agent's vfunc +16 returns true (decompile).
UIMessageBanner_Show (sub_140111D20; proposed name) resolves the node named Title on the banner object (decompile).
BattleMsg_IdFromDescriptor (BattleMsg_IdFromDescriptor): class 0 subtype 2 -> 1000 x kind + (word & 0x7FF) for the kinds in registry BattleMsgKindBase, any other descriptor -> 0xFFFFFFFF (decompile).

BattleMsg_TextFromDescriptor (sub_1400FCBB4): class 0 subtype 2 -> the message text of the id from step 3; class 1 subtype 27 -> UIText_Get(word); class 1 subtype 171 -> the table-172 text of word; anything else null (decompile).
CMesId_GetText (CMesId_GetText) reads the row named by the message id from NXD table 172 through g_CMesIdTable; a missing row gives null (decompile).

BattleMsg_FillArgs (sub_1401EC074) resets the format-argument vector and either calls BattleMsg_BuildArgs for the descriptor or copies up to 40 stored entries from the message object at a 524-byte stride (decompile).

BattleMsg_BuildArgs (BattleMsg_BuildArgs) switches on the message id and pushes the arguments that fill the template's <string=lstrN> and <num=...> markers, read from the battle message record; for message id 10098 the item name, for 10141 and 10145 and up the actor name and a status or ability value (decompile).

UIMessageBanner_Show calls GUITextNode_SetTextExpanded with the template and the argument vector at 0x140111E98; it substitutes the arguments into the markers and the node ends with the expanded string (GUITextNode_SetString is called from inside it) (decompile, live trace 2026-10-31).

The banner function stores the expanded text on the node; with no descriptor or with enable clear it stores the literal ? instead. It then picks the banner state from the object's +80 (1 ParameterUp, 2 ParameterDown, 3 Item, 4 Trap, 5 TreasureBoxCrystal, 6 DestroySteal, 7..8 the NineGrid variants) and starts it (decompile).
The text node is laid out before it is drawn (GUITextNode_Layout); the exact call site in this path was not traced.
GUITextNode_Draw draws the node; it returns before emitting anything when one of its four gate conditions fails (decompile and disassembly; see the behavior TextNodeDrawGate).

notes: Steps 1-7 name functions whose sheets are separate; the proposed names are used here. M (owner observation 2026-10-31): the same bubble style also serves the level-up banner and the select-a-facing-direction prompt.
open_questions: ? what triggers each of the two battle message handlers; ? the producer of the descriptor for an ability cast; ? whether the state at +80 follows the message kind or the caller.

name: BattleResumeRestoresTheLooks
summary: How a battle resumed from a payload gets its looks back: the setup clears the pool's sprite bytes, the payload fills the snapshot region, and Battle_RestoreSceneVars copies the units, the load queue and the 15 pool records back from it.

members.text: Battle setup: sets byte +1 of all 15 pool records to 0 (0x140210BF9) and byte +1 of every battle unit to 0xFF.
Only when the load mode dword 0x142FF9E2C is 1: when sub_14021849C returns non-zero, sub_1402181EC materialises the resume payload.
A payload of kind 1 is copied (668,112 bytes) into the snapshot region at 0x1408167A0, which holds g_UnitLookPoolIndex, g_UnitSceneSlotIndex and g_SnapshotLookPool.
Scene variables, live stores, the 21 battle units, the load queue with its count and the 15 pool records are copied back from the region.
Then g_UnitSceneSlotIndex is set to -1 (memset of 0x54 bytes) and the ten g_LookPoolFaceValue dwords to -1.
On the resume path (mode 1) a scene unit takes its slot from g_UnitSceneSlotIndex and its pool index from g_UnitLookPoolIndex by the unit index +444.

open_questions: ? how g_UnitSceneSlotIndex gets its entries back between step 5 and step 6 (sub_14026A048 reads it); ? whether the restored queue entries (unit pointers of the saving process; the exe has a dynamic base) are consumed or the units are queued anew.

name: BattleTimelineCameraFlow
summary: The four-step camera sequence of the battle timeline's focus screen. The battle frame update calls `Battle_TimelineFocusCamera` once per frame while `g_BattleState` is 91; the shared step word `dword_140D3A86C` selects placement of the timeline on the acting unit (0), the wait for the panel's first transition (1), the interactive scroll and range preview while action 0xDB is active (2), or the wait for the panel's second transition and the dispatch of the next queued battle state (3). State 3 pops that record, which writes its +16 to `g_BattleState` and its +20 to the step word; the focus then either confirms the queued state 4 or runs a short closing sequence through `Battle_TimelineRefresh`. It never pushes or pops a task of its own.

members.text: The battle frame update (`sub_140210AF0`) calls the focus step in battle state 91. The timeline entry `sub_1402095FC` sets the step word `dword_140D3A86C` to 0 and the counter `dword_140D40464` to 0; the battle command dispatch `sub_140208BE4` can instead reload the step word from the queued record's +20 field and write its +16 to `g_BattleState`.
State 0 resolves the unit under the three cursor tile coordinates (0x140C6AFB8/0x140C6ADAC/0x140C6AFBC). The lookup prefers the current actor when more than one scene object matches.

State 0 scans `g_TurnList` for the unit's entry. It puts the entry on row 4 when the list index allows, sets the scroll to index - 4 and clamps it at 31; low indices use row = index and scroll = 0, high indices use row = index - 31 and scroll = 31.

When the focused row holds a unit, state 0 starts presentation script 1, waits a frame, moves the cursor onto that unit and waits a second frame before guide page 109 is shown. The script is a battle presentation program; the focus step itself still returns to the frame update.

State 0 increments the counter and, on the pass where it reaches 5, calls the panel transition helper with 0 (I: the +57192 transition) and sets the step word to 1. State 0 therefore runs six passes. State 1 resets the counter and waits until the +57192 state stops running.

State 2 follows action 0xDB, the input that opens the timeline from the map cursor. While the input is active, the scroll helper `sub_14010F27C` moves the row and scroll and the step redraws the focused unit. When the input is not active, the step peeks the next queued battle record, calls the panel transition helper with -1 (I: the +57368 transition) and sets the step word to 3.
On a state-2 redraw, an entry whose first byte has bit 0x40 set and bit 0x20 clear gets the pending action's range shape applied to the cursor mask, after the cursor moves onto the unit's area.

State 3 waits for the +57368 state to stop, dispatches the next queued battle record (`sub_140208BE4`, which writes the record's +16 to `g_BattleState` and its +20 to the step word), starts presentation script 2 with the unit record's byte +444 as the actor slot, and handles the queued state id: 13 plays the two-state UI animation at 0, 23 plays it at -1, and 4 goes to the confirm dispatch.

`BattleAction_ConfirmCommand` resolves the cursor unit and chooses one of three handlers. I: two handlers set `g_BattleState` to 4, the third sets it to 5, and all three start presentation script 3 (rests on the handler bodies, outside this function).

When the confirm leaves `g_BattleState` at 4, the step sets the camera scale `dword_1407DC2BC` to 1 and returns without waiting a frame; the next battle frame dispatches state 4. Any other result falls into the closing sequence.

The closing sequence (also taken by every other result) sets the timeline-mode sentinel `dword_140D4058C` to -1, calls the timeline refresh, pauses input for 0.1 s, starts script 1, holds one frame, refreshes the guide, waits a second frame and returns. It does not restore the previous state or step word; the next frame dispatches whatever `g_BattleState` holds after the dispatch and confirm.
The refresh takes its 40-entry forecast from this builder before copying it into `g_TurnList` and filling the visible panel rows.

behavior.text: the focus is one of the battle frame update's state handlers: `g_BattleState` 90 and 97 run the timeline screen `sub_140209218`, 91 runs this four-step camera sequence, and 92 and 93 run further handlers that use the same step word.

the step word `dword_140D3A86C` is shared with the timeline screen and with the battle load machine; it is not a private sub-state. The timeline entry sets it to 0, and the battle command dispatch reloads it from the queued record's +20 field and writes the record's +16 to `g_BattleState`.
state 0 is the placement pass: it scans `g_TurnList` for the acting unit, puts it on row 4 where the index allows, sets the scroll, and starts script 1 only when the focused row holds a unit.

state 1 waits for the panel's first transition (+57192); state 2 follows action 0xDB and previews the focused row's range; state 3 waits for the panel's second transition (+57368) and dispatches the next queued battle state.

the queued state id 4 goes through `BattleAction_ConfirmCommand`; the dispatch has already written 4 to `g_BattleState`, and the handlers may leave it at 4 or set it to 5. The focus treats only 4 as success.
the closing sequence rebuilds the timeline panel through `Battle_TimelineRefresh`, pauses input, plays script 1 and returns after two frames. It does not roll back `g_BattleState` or the step word.

the sequence never pushes or pops a task of its own. Every case returns to the battle frame update; the next frame dispatches the state that state 3's record or the confirm handlers wrote, with the step word from the record. The presentation scripts started along the way run through `BattleAction_StartScript`.
the four steps are one camera sequence: place, settle, scroll and confirm, finalise. (rests on the two panel state nodes, the action 0xDB test and the confirm dispatch.)
the queued state id 4 is the confirm path and 13/23 are the two timeline guide states. (rests on the three confirm handlers and on the two guide-animation calls.)
what queued state ids 13 and 23 name; what `dword_140D3A840` selects; what the queued record's +24 field selects.

notes: Covers the focus function, the two timeline entry functions, the command dispatch, the three confirm handlers, the panel scroll helper and the two cursor-camera helpers. Addresses are build-specific.
open_questions: ? what queued state ids 13 and 23 name; ? what `dword_140D3A840` selects; ? what the queued record's +24 field selects.

name: BattleVoiceLine
summary: How a battle event becomes a spoken voice cue: suppress test, status gate, chance roll, replacement, play or queue.

members.text: An ability line is chosen from the Ability row's voice list by the request phase.
A replaceable line is swapped for row 3 or 2 by the request flags.
Side test: a non-zero result stops the line.
Status gate: statuses that forbid speech stop the line (line 21 always passes).
Skipped while fast-forward runs; rolls the group chance.
Chance in percent of the line's column in the speaker's group row.
Cue number, with the three replacement rows.
A delayed cue is queued and played when its delay has run out.

notes: The pattern of each controller is set by BattleVoice_AssignPatterns and BattleVoice_SetPattern when a unit is built.
open_questions: ? who builds the request.

name: BootStateMachine
summary: The boot dispatcher's states 0..4 and the 5..7 hand-over codes. State 0 loads the settings and the save data, state 1 is the confirm skip, state 2 runs the video/title frame and owns the task threads, state 3 plays a movie, and state 4 is the Enhanced/Classic launcher. A change runs the old state's exit actions before the new state's entry actions.

members.text: `sub_1401E7EF8` loads the config and settings; it walks its own 0..7 sub-state through the loader slot (`sub_1403D2940`), the NXD registry check, the settings file and the save manager. I: the move to state 4 is made through `sub_1401E7C0C`, the recorded `Boot_SetState` caller for state 4 (no direct call from `sub_1401E7EF8` appears in the cross-references).

The dispatcher tests action 81 (confirm) and calls `Boot_SetState(2)`; the state also resets the UI state object's screen size and surface. No boot code calls `Boot_SetState(1)` in this build, so the state is never entered.
The video/title state: at sub-state 0 it starts the task threads, then runs the video body and either starts a movie (3), returns to the launcher (4) or takes the exit flag to the hand-over code 7.
Plays the requested movie; on the end conditions it calls `Boot_SetState` with the previous-state mirror, returning to the state that started the movie (state 2 in the video path).
The Enhanced/Classic launcher: startup screen, title cushion and launcher. Result 1 calls `Boot_SetState(2)`, result 2 starts the Classic program, 3 runs the load route and 4 opens the options.
No handler in `Boot_Frame` and no writer in the executable; not decoded.
No handler in `Boot_Frame` and no writer in the executable; not decoded.
Hand-over code written only by `Boot_UpdateVideo` when `dword_142E7FB00` is non-zero; `Boot_Frame` has no branch and returns before its frame tail.

behavior.text: order inside one change: the old state's exit switch runs first, then the three state writes, then the new state's entry switch.

state 2 owns the task threads: `Boot_UpdateVideo` starts them with `Boot_StartThreads`; `Boot_SetState`'s entry 2 only refreshes the video state. I: the state-2 exit destroys the manager only when no movie is requested and `dword_142E7FB00` is 0 (the code compares the 64-bit value at `dword_142E7FB00` with 0xFFFFFFFF00000000).
the initial state is 0: the boot init `sub_1400B532C` writes 0 and the variable starts zeroed in the data segment.
state 4 is the only state that allocates a boot UI object; its exit frees the object and closes the add-ons.
the two mirrors are written on every change: `dword_1407829E8` keeps the previous state and is read by `Boot_MovieFrame`; `dword_1407829E4` keeps the new state and has no reader.
states 5 and 6 are unused numbers, and 7 is an exit code rather than a state the dispatcher can run (rests on the missing branches and call sites).

notes: State handler addresses: 0 `sub_1401E7EF8` (0x1401E7EF8), 1 the confirm test in `Boot_Frame`, 2 `Boot_UpdateVideo` (0x1402561D0), 3 `Boot_MovieFrame` (0x1402F2E40), 4 `Boot_Update` (0x1401DE164).
open_questions: What states 5 and 6 were meant for; what sets `dword_142E7FB00`; and what leaves `dword_140D3A8D4` at 0 when state 2 is entered so the thread factory runs.

name: BootToGameThread
summary: The hand-over from boot to the game's task threads: boot state 2 creates 17 task threads, installs the game-thread entry in the task-0 command slot, then stops the boot dispatcher. The entry runs on a task thread and reaches the game's outer loop; the Win32 message pump stays on the main thread.

members.text: Boot state 2 with display sub-state 0: the handler polls `sub_1403D2940` and calls `Boot_StartThreads` only on a return of 0.
Creates 17 TaskThread objects in the manager block (96-byte stride, 0x60000 stacks) and starts them through `sub_14006A67C`.
Installs `sub_140348658` in the task-0 command slot at 0x143791D78, sets the scheduler flags and leaves the display sub-state at 2.

When `dword_142E7FB00` is non-zero the same handler fades out and calls `Boot_SetState(7)`; `Boot_Frame` then returns without its tail, so the boot dispatcher stops. `dword_142E7FB00` is non-zero on this path, so the state-2 exit does not destroy the task manager.
Each task thread runs `sub_140037BD8` then `sub_1402F3698`; that loop copies the slot at +8 into +0 and calls the copy, so task 0 executes the installed entry.

name: CursorGloveFrame
summary: What happens to the finger cursor's glove in one UI frame, in order: its Loop clock advances, scrubs the Hand's Loop, the Hand's IconHand position is sampled as an integer, and the cursor reference node glides toward the focused panel. The two integers meet only in the node matrices.

members.text: Start of the UI frame: the UI time ui+13480 = dt * g_UIDataModule+28 (1.0), dt being the application's frame time (at least 1/60 s).
Only when a show is pending (show_state 2): the restart runs now and ends in UIAddonFingerCursor_PlayLoop: the Loop clock of the main component is zeroed, running, dirty, looping.
Loop state: time = frame = prev_frame = 0, loop flag 1, running and dirty set; nothing is applied to nodes here.
The agent update: the cursor reference node moves one glide step (integer, roundf) toward the focused panel's rect; independent of the Loop clock.
g_GUICore+2100 = the UI time.
The widget tick: dt = 0 when a block bit is set, else g_GUICore+2100 (selector 0) or +2104 (selector 1).
Calls the main component's virtual +32, GUIComponent_Update.

The component handles the event: the child CursorRef's Loop state is enabled, paused, and its frame = min(max((frame - 0) * 40 / (40 - 0), 0), 40), time = frame / 60, dirty.

IconHand's position track: key search on the truncated frame, u and the curve in single precision, the result truncated toward zero to an integer pair.

Node matrices: IconHand local = (pivot + position) - scale * pivot; times the Layer00 node (offset -86, -17) and the cursor reference node (the glide position) and the layer transform. No rounding anywhere in this chain.

behavior.text: steps 8 to 13 run on the UI frame time; step 4 has no time term.
the first tick after a restart advances the Loop to about frame 1 before anything is applied (step 3 applies nothing, step 8 moves the frame).

Live read points: global qword_143CD9DA8 (addon manager) +16 = agent vector, element 1 = the agent (UIAgentCursor); agent +0x40 = the addon (UIAddonFingerCursor); addon +0x18 = the widget; widget +104 .. +112 = component pointers, the first with +536 = 1 is the main component; its states are the vector at +616 .. +624 (state +0 = the name text pointer, compare with the text Loop): time +0x4C, frame +0x50, previous frame +0x54, flags +0x68 .. +0x6F. name: EquipSessionFlagFlow
summary: The Outfitter/equip session: build candidates, buy or apply a slot word with bit 15, then commit (strip the bit, charge the price, save) or cancel (restore the override).

members.text: The screen table entry runs sub_1402BE7E8 and then the per-frame dispatcher sub_1402D6F10; sub_1402D5CC4 builds the candidate array for the selected unit.

Shop_BuildItemList is called with mode 2 (only equippable items), the five category lists are merged into the 152-word stack list, and each of the first four output words is OR-ed with 0x8000 when it differs from the unit word and the override word.
A candidate with bit 14 is refused (0x1402D72A0); otherwise the current slot is removed, the new price is added to dword_143D1AC68 and the unit word is written as id | 0x8000.
The leave path writes the candidate (which may carry bit 15) to the unit word, adjusts dword_143D1AC68 for every changed slot, calls PartyUnit_ReloadEquipment and closes the screen state.

The commit message (0x3D) runs sub_1402D65D4 over every party unit: a word at or above 0x4000 is masked with 0x3FF, its override is returned to the inventory and cleared; then sub_140285A6C writes every unit to the save.
The cancel messages (0 and 6) run sub_1402D5B6C: a word at or above 0x4000, or a non-zero override, is replaced by the override; every override word is cleared.
Every slot change and every commit rebuilds the 64-byte panel block at 0x141876E90 from the unit and save records; the hand words reach the block raw.

behavior.text: bit 15 is the session flag, not the item-present flag: a committed item is stored without it and 0 is the empty slot.
bit 14 is produced on list entries by Shop_BuildItemList and Inventory_BuildEquipList, is refused by sub_1402D7280, and is not produced on any candidate or party hand word by a stock writer.
the commit order is strip (sub_1402D65D4), save (sub_140285A6C), then screen refresh (JobScreen_RefreshAfterChange); the cancel order restores and does not save.

name: ItemMenuListLifecycle

members.text: Town loop and Poachers' Den loop: each accepted id is stored as one word; in mode 1 an id the unit cannot equip gets 0x4000 ORed in first (constant loaded at 0x140288F12 and 0x140288FF5, stores at 0x140288FC4 and 0x140289068). The mark is set only with a unit and mode 1.
Equip list: the same mark through a bit-set of bit 14 at 0x140288CAF, stored at 0x140288CB6, mode 1 only; modes 2 and above drop the refused id instead and mode 0 never asks.

Called by the screens' list builders right after a mode-1 build (ShopList_BuildEntries at 0x14036B1EB, sub_1403368C0 at 0x14033695A) and by Inventory_BuildEquipList itself for the order-list groups: it rewrites g_MenuList in the saved order and drops the ids that order does not name, so the position of a word in the list changes after the producers have stored it.
Reads the list word of each displayed row; the word only feeds the entry's cannot-equip byte (shift by 14, AND 1). Mark only.
Row count: masks the word to an id for Item_CountTotal, then tests bit 14 afterwards. Id and mark.
Equipped count: the same shape, an AND with 0x4000 afterwards. Id and mark.
Price: the same shape with Item_GetRecord. Id and mark.
Memory test of 0x4000 on a list word, then a branch. Mark only.
Memory test of 0x4000 on a list word at 0x140333C5D, then a branch. Mark only.
Ability popup: a bit-14 test (0x14036732C) whose register is not used afterwards; on an ability list the bit means 'cannot learn', so this reader never sees an item.

behavior.text: the three writers are the only item producers of g_MenuList (Shop_BuildItemList twice, Inventory_BuildEquipList once); nothing reads the word between the instruction that sets the mark and the store.

the seven readers are the functions that test bit 14 of a list word (the list above, steps 4 to 10); a scan of the 127 functions that call an item helper (Item_GetRecord, Item_CountTotal, Item_MenuCategory, Item_CanUnitEquip, Inventory_AddCount, Item_CountEquippedByParty, Item_SellPrice, Item_IsValidId) found no other bit-14 or bit-15 test on an item list word; the rest of the hits are random numbers, button masks and a battle message flag on a byte id.

a possession-list word (0x141D32F00) has two readers that test 0x4000 and a Classic item-use page; by static callers they are reached only from the Classic item pages (ClassicItemUsePage_Run, ClassicItemListPage_Run and two helpers, entered from data tables), so no Enhanced screen reaches them by a direct call.

name: ItemNameToScreen
summary: How an item id becomes a name on screen, by two independent routes: the 0x3800 text id (a pool id decoded by sub_140226208, carried in a 2-byte list cell or a 32-bit message argument) and the Item-en row lookup (ItemTable_GetName, a full 32-bit key). The route decides the id width and whether the string is a pool entry or a table row.

members.text: A builder adds the tag to an item id: 0x3800 for the name pool, 0x6800 for the help pool. There are 12 name-tag sites in 11 functions (mostly 16-bit ids, one 8-bit) and 7 help sites in 6 functions.
The tagged word is stored in a list cell (2 bytes, tag in bits 15..11) or as a 32-bit argument in the current-message block 0x140783210 or the shared help slot 0x1418736B4.
A consumer splits the word: kind = bits 15..11, index = bits 10..0. The item branches test kind 7 and recover the id with an 11-bit mask.
The pool decoder looks the kind up in qword_140D40990 and walks the index-th record of that pool. Kinds 14 and 22 are redirected; there is no bounds check.

The text command's callback receives the id at 32 bits (the posting thunk sign-extends it), calls the decoder and attaches the string to the node. A second callback uses the duplicate decoder EventText_FindMessage.
The other route: the Item-en row (nxd table 45) by the full 32-bit item id. ItemCell_BindIconAndName and the name branch of sub_140153CA0 call it directly and never form a text id.
The cell sets icon path and name only when the Item-en row exists and the id is not negative; with no row it leaves the cell unset.
The list picture is built from the same id, unmasked, and bound with the name; the picture path has its own format record (ItemIconPath).

behavior.text: the carriers differ in width. The list cell is 2 bytes; the current-message block, the text command and the help slot carry 32 bits with no 16-bit store; the battle message queue's item branch keeps only the low 8 bits of its value when bit 15 is set.
the tag arithmetic is the limit: 0x3800 + N changes kind for N >= 0x800, and 0x6800 + N becomes the ability kind 0x7000. The Item-en accessor takes the full 32-bit id; only its callers mask.

the name and the help have different sources. The name may come from Item-en (panels) or pool 7 (text ids); the help may be pool 13 (a 0x6800 token) or the Item-en description field (the equipment detail panel).

notes: V: the decode points are the generic decoder, the battle-name masks, the cell id mask and the tag builders.

name: NxdMultiKeyLookup

By (key1, key2): binary search of the bound entries (NxdEntries_Search2); triple keyed: the first leaf of child (key1, key2).
By (key1, key2, key3): binary search of the bound entries (NxdEntries_Search3).

A whole set: the entry of its first record and the set's count; callers walk consecutive bound entries.
A set's record count (double: rows; triple: children); UITable_GetRowCount wraps it.
The row: record + its row offset (+8 double, +16 triple).

The NexResourceHandle with NxdTable_BindRows as the load callback and NxdTable_OnReady as the ready callback, both with the table as context.

Reader and resolved path released; the buffer stays with the handle until the handle is released (ResourceHandle_FreeData).
Every later lookup: by position (contiguous keys) or binary search over the entries.

name: OpeningStages

The skip paths in tasks 4, 5 and 6 end through `Opening_EndToTitle`; task 7 clears the flag as it starts the title.

members.text: Mode-0 scene entry: selects UI row 0x11 (row 0 when `g_ShopModeGate` is non-zero), ends any pending fade transition, sets bit 1 and clears bit 6 of `dword_141876EE8`, and pushes task id 0 on the current task stack, initialising the first two dwords of its 100-byte frame.

Loads the two opening message textures, selects the language's opening sprite list, resets the opening text flags with `sub_14037FC0C`, pushes task id 4 and writes 0 to its state field at frame +0x10.

With `g_ShopModeGate` zero, state 0 waits for `sub_14039DF20`; state 4 runs the opening menu loop `sub_14037B144`. A matching menu result or `dword_142E7FF5C` sets state 5, which pops task 4 and pushes task 7; otherwise task 4 pops itself and `sub_14037E1E8` pushes task 5. A set skip flag moves to state 99 and then 100, ending through `Opening_EndToTitle`.

name: OpeningToTitle
summary: The opening's route to the title and back. A mode-0 scene start loads the opening page and pushes task 0; task 0 waits for any requested movie, then starts the title scene (task 14). The title's New Game hand-off (result 1 -> task 15 -> row 1 -> task 1) leaves through task 1, the exit gate; the scripted stage chain (4 -> 5 -> 6 -> 1) is separate and has no established entry. Task 13, pushed from the title, restarts the mode-0 opening from the same first task.

members.text: Mode 0: clears the page index, resets the scene flags and the task depth, and calls `OpeningScene_Start`.

Loads opening row 17, or row 0 on the `g_ShopModeGate` path where it may also show the title menu; clears flag bit 6, sets bit 1, ends any pending UI fade, pushes id 0 and writes 86999 and 10261 to the first scene frame.
While `g_MovieRequestId` is 0 or greater the task returns and stays on top. When it is -1 it clears bit 1, pops itself and calls `TitleScene_Start`.
`TitleScene_Start` resets the scene state, builds the title menu and pushes task 14 (`TitleScene_Task`). Task 0 never pushes an opening stage.
The New Game hand-off: the helper `sub_1402F0084` loads opening row 1, clears flag bit 6 and pushes task 1. Task 15 (pushed by case 1 of `TitleScene_Task`) and task 6 call it.
Task 1 clears bit 1 when no movie is requested, pops itself, sets bit 6 and either calls `Opening_EndToTitle` (byte `g_GlobalWork+100` set) or writes hand-over code 0 and toggles the run bit (bit 0).
The scripted stage chain (separate pages) is 4 -> 5 -> 6 -> 1; task 7 is the return-to-title shortcut from task 4 state 5. The chain has no established entry in this build (no store of id 2 or 12).
Releases the three opening objects, clears bit 0 of `dword_143C51A40`, calls `Scene_Init(1)` (title start, task 14), then clears the two scene words and the qword after `g_ScreenFadeMode`.
Task 13, selected by case 3 of `TitleScene_Task`, sets bit 6, clears the page index, pops itself and re-enters `OpeningScene_Start`, which pushes task 0 again.

behavior.text: the mode-0 start and the stage chain are separate entry paths: task 0 always goes to `TitleScene_Start`, and task 1 is pushed by `sub_1402F0084`, not by task 0.
task 1 and `Opening_EndToTitle` are the two exits: task 1 leaves with hand-over code 0 unless `g_GlobalWork+100` is set, and `Opening_EndToTitle` resets the scene into the title.
`OpeningScene_Resume` does not restore a frame: it resets the page index and re-enters the same start function, which always pushes id 0 and writes the same two frame dwords.

a scan of the stores to `dword_1418772E0` finds ids 0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14 and 15; no store of 2 or 12 was found. The helper that pushes 4 is called only by tasks 2 and 12, and the helper that pushes 3 only by task 2, so the route into the 4-7 chain is not established in this build.
the title is the hub: the mode-0 start lands there through task 0, the opening stages return there through `Opening_EndToTitle`, and task 13 comes back from it (rests on the three paths).
what the two frame dwords mean; what `g_GlobalWork+100` selects; and what title action leads to case 3.

notes: Read the five assigned functions whole, plus `Scene_Init`, `TitleScene_Start`, `TitleScene_Task`, `sub_14037F354`, `sub_1402F0084`, `sub_1402F0C14` and the stage functions around their pushes and ends. Task 0 does not push task 1; task 1 is pushed by `sub_1402F0084`.

name: OpeningTransitionTasks
summary: The hand-off tasks between the front end's three loops. The title's New Game result pushes task 15, which loads opening row 1 and task 1; the title's idle result pushes task 11, which waits out a demo movie and re-enters the opening start; the alternate loop starts at task 9, which requests PSP movie row 0x10, and task 10 closes its screen and clears the run bit. Task 12 is the opening's skip/continue gate, but no store of id 12 exists, so it does not run in this build.

members.text: Result 1 (New Game): pops task 14, runs `sub_14037FF14(0)` and `LegacyMenu_InitWorld`, loads PSP movie row 0x15 and pushes task 15.
Task 15 waits while `g_MovieRequestId` is 0 or greater, pops itself, sets the page index to 1 and calls `sub_1402F0084`, which loads PSP movie row 1 and pushes task 1.

Task 1 waits for the movie, then either writes hand-over code 0 and toggles bit 0 of `dword_141876EE8` (normally set, so this clears it), or ends to the title through `Opening_EndToTitle` when `g_GlobalWork+100` is set.

Result 4 (idle timeout): the title task loads PSP movie row 18, 19 or 20, sets scene flag bit 1 and pushes task 11. Task 11 waits for that movie, pops itself, sets the page index to 1 and re-enters `OpeningScene_Start`.

Loads PSP movie row 17 (row 0 when `g_ShopModeGate` is set), sets scene flag bit 1, ends the UI fade and pushes task 0. Task 0 waits for the movie, pops and starts the title scene, so the idle path is a loop back to task 14.
The alternate loop resets the scene words inline, loads the 0x8800-byte data run, requests PSP movie row 9, pushes task 9 and runs the same dispatch until scene flag bit 0 clears.
Task 9 clears scene flag bit 1 when no movie is pending, sets bit 6, pops itself, requests PSP movie row 0x10, writes event id 16 and pushes task 10.

Task 10 waits while `g_MovieRequestId` is 0 or greater, fades the +400 UI screen to state 15, waits for its state 4/1, detaches the add-on, releases three pointers and toggles scene flag bit 0, which ends the loop when it runs.

The gate that is not entered: with no fade running it offers cancel (script id 0x1B) or accept (0x1A or 0x1F); cancel refills the scene buffer and calls `TitleScene_Start`, accept calls `Opening_LoadMessageSprites`, which pushes task 4. No store of id 12 exists.

behavior.text: the title has four result paths: result 1 pushes 15, result 2 ends the scene and writes the hand-over code, result 3 replaces the top id with 13, and result 4 pushes 11.
task 15 -> `sub_1402F0084` -> task 1 is the New Game hand-off; task 11 -> `OpeningScene_Start` -> task 0 is the idle/attract return.
the alternate loop is the only path that starts at task 9; task 9 always pushes 10, and task 10 is the only task in that loop that toggles scene flag bit 0.
ids 8 and 12 have no store site. Ids 2 and 12 are the only table handlers that enter the stage chain 4-7, so that chain is not reached from either loop in this build.
task 10's first test is `g_MovieRequestId`, not the adjacent `dword_142E7FB00` the decompiler prints.

task 10's exit tail is the loop's intended end, but the three pointers it releases are never written and start at -1, so whether the tail runs is open (rests on the -1 initial values and the release helper's pointer use).
which movies rows 0x10, 1, 17, 18, 19 and 20 are; why the event id is 16; and whether the alternate loop runs for every transition mode 3.

notes: Read the six group-B handlers whole, plus `TitleScene_Task`, `TitleScene_Start`, `TitleScene_Update`, `OpeningScene_Start`, `OpeningTask_0`, `OpeningTask_1`, `OpeningTask_4`, `OpeningTask_7`, `SceneLoop_RunAlt`, `sub_1402F0084` and the store sites of the task ids. The title's result meanings rest on the agent state words 0x0101/0x0201/0x0301/0x0401/0x0701 written by the title screens and on the stage switch in `TitleScene_Update`. `OpeningTask_0`, `OpeningTask_1` and `OpeningTask_4` are referenced here only for the hand-off.
open_questions: Which movie rows the four title hand-offs request; what the `g_GlobalWork+100` byte selects at task 1; and whether the alternate-loop tail is reachable as shipped.

name: PartyMenuFaceChain
summary: How a party unit's face reaches a menu with enhanced graphics: the save record's marker and job give a look index, the index a portrait code, the code a byte and a colour, the byte a face number through the face table, and the face number a texture name. Every step after the code is a byte, so at most 256 faces can come out of a code.

members.text: A screen asks for a unit's face: mode 1 when both dwords of qword_142FF9F30 are 0 (party list, job screen and status headers, errand result); mode 0 goes to the battle pool path (sub_140214134).
Scene ids 21, 43, 44 and 51 take the selector branch (scene unit entries, SceneUnit_EntryById); every other scene takes the save-record branch with index below 0x36.
Look index from the marker: below 0x80 itself, 0x80 / 0x81 2 * job - 52 / - 51, 0x82 job row +46, 0xA2 / 0xA3 fixed; index below 0xD3 reads the code word of copy F.
A code with bit 8 or 9 set is refused (-1); marker 0x82 adds job row +47 << 10 (colour bits).
The classic atlas cell of the code's low byte and the colour 8 + bits 10..11; returns the low byte.
No code (-1): the record index stands in for it. The unmapped value goes to g_HdFaceSlotValues[0] and g_DialogueFaceSlot0; the UI table 0x112 row of the marker adjusts the colour.
Below 2.0 the function returns -1 (no face from this path).

When g_FaceDisplayMode & ~2 is 0 the code becomes a face number through g_SpriteIdToShape (or SpriteId_ToShape's list); an unmapped code is returned as it is; then the cap 0xCD (0x1402C0816) turns a larger answer into -1.
The face widget takes the face number and colour (the party list's sub_1402C1EA8).
A few numbers up to 205 are replaced; every other number passes.
The name: UI texture path row 4 formatted with %d face and colour; then GUIWidget_EnsureSlotGroup(name).

behavior.text: the classic-graphics portrait goes another way: PartyUnit_GetFaceRecord's +8 word is rebuilt from PartyUnit_BuildJobRecord's code as atlas cell ((code >> 2) + 224) << 6, wrapped with & 0x1FF from 512 up.

name: SaveFrameStep
summary: How a manual save or load reaches the file: the save screen changes a command, and one frame step does the work once per frame, blocking that frame while the container is read or written. Store, load and image-to-cache are the three cases of the same step; the UI never touches the container.

members.text: A save, delete or import callback sets the command on the save-I/O state (1 store, 2 load, 3 image to cache) and returns; the screen keeps reading the cache.
The frame update calls the step once per frame; it reads the command and runs exactly one case.
Case 1: the 50-slot cache is copied into the manager image and queued as the `fftsave.bin` entry; the PNG write is requested on the request object.
Case 2 first probes the area file; when it is absent the command is cleared and no load happens (an absent file is no save data, not an error).
Case 2: the image is filled with the empty-slot pattern and the entry is requested; the container is read and the payload delivered before the step returns.
Case 3: the manager image is copied into the cache (2,008,200 bytes), which is how a freshly loaded or imported image reaches the list.
The step ends at the reset path, which sets the command back to 0; nothing runs until a callback sets it again (the absent-file path does this explicitly).

behavior.text: one case per frame, and a load that spans a container read completes inside that same step (the read is synchronous).
the step is the only place the cache and the container meet, so answering store and load there leaves the rest of the save screen untouched.
the load case probes the area file, not the entry, so a container without the entry also ends with an empty list and no dialog.
everything in the step runs on the game thread inside the frame update, so a replacement may block the frame exactly as the game does.

notes: The frame update reaches the step once per frame; the save, load and delete callbacks run in the same update, so the command is normally set and consumed in different frames.
open_questions: ? what sets the sub-state at +0x108 within a step that needs more than one frame.

name: SaveLoadScreenFlow
summary: The save/load screen's ordered path. One UI agent opens behind a fade, shows a saving overlay while it loads the save index, creates the list addon, builds the automatic rows and the tab, then rests in state 0 while the list addon sends events. The events branch to load, save, erase, the New Game + source pick, the close path, or a deferred switch that waits before entering the load or source-pick state.

members.text: Opens the screen: clears the low three mode bits and sets mode 2, starts BGM transition 8, requests fade state 9 and sets the agent to state 1. It pushes no scene task.

Agent state 1 (registry entry UISaveLoad_StateSavingOverlay): allocates the 80-byte UIAddonSaving overlay, attaches it, stores it at +0x630 and loads UI row 256 into it. Phase 1 waits for the save-data manager to be idle, sub_1400C480C to return 0 and the overlay's +0x44 byte to be set; then agent state 2.

Agent state 2 (sub_1401836F0): sets the second state block at +0x68 to state 1 and runs its phase 1; when that block reaches state 2 it sets agent state 3. The block's state-3 table slot is a no-op and no code writes it.

Second-block state 1: calls SaveSlots_LoadFromFile(g_SaveManager), which loads the fftsave.bin entry into the save manager image, and sets the save-I/O word at qword_140D405B8+0x104 to 3. Phase 1 waits for sub_1400C3790() to return 0 and then sets the block to state 2.

Agent state 3: allocates the 1240-byte UIAddonFFTOSaveLoad addon, attaches it and stores it at +0x628. When mode bit 1 is set (mode 2) it resets the header counter and asks the save-data manager for slot 0; phase 1 copies one 264-byte FFTI header per request into +0x100+n*0x108 until five are collected, then enters state 4. Other modes enter state 4 at once.

Agent state 4: requests the saving overlay close, selects the tab from the mode bits (mode 1 -> tab 0, mode 2 -> tab 1, mode 4 -> tab 2), clears focus, builds the automatic rows from the five headers, writes the tab at list_addon+0x1B0, loads UI row 252 into the list addon and sets its active byte at +0x4D1. Phase 1 waits for the overlay to hide and returns to agent state 0.

The list addon's bind/refresh virtual calls SaveLoadList_Refresh. It rebuilds the list for the tab at +0x1B0, sets the auto/manual filter to 0 on tab 1 and -1 on tabs 0 and 2, shows either the rows or the layout's ShowTextNone state, updates the three filter buttons and finishes on the guide bar.

SaveLoadList_BuildEntries rebuilds vector A for the current tab and sorts it: tab 0 adds one entry created by sub_140186390 and then every valid cache slot; tab 1 copies the automatic-entry vector and then every valid cache slot; tab 2 adds only valid slots whose byte at record +0x119 is non-zero and whose situation byte at +0x11A is 5 or 0.

The agent is now in state 0 and the list addon handles input. Its item-action virtual sends 1 or 4 on the auto tab, 3 or 5 on the New Game + tab and 2, 6 or 8 on the manual tab; its input virtual sends 0 on back and 7 on action 0xFB. Events 0..3 are accepted only in state 0; events 4..8 open pause-style prompts in any state.

Load (agent state 5; published as sub_1401839E4, IDB name UISaveLoad_StateLoad): phase 0 clears focus, resets the scene state, calls the music helper for track 8 in mode 2, requests fade 9, asks the overlay to open, and either calls sub_1400C4214(slot, 1) when +0xF4 is set or SaveSlot_LoadToLive(slot); it detaches the list addon. Phase 1 waits for the fade and the save request and closes the overlay. Phase 2 calls Save_ResumeCheckpoint when +0xF4 is set, otherwise sub_140257354 only when the slot's +0x11A byte is 1, then sets g_GlobalWork+102, dword_142E80228 and g_GlobalWork+104 to 1, calls sub_140182E7C, frees the System agent's addons and calls sub_140151B34 on agent slot 19 (the UIAgentAnnounce object, vector begin + 152).

Save (agent state 6): phase 0 marks the list active, clears focus, calls SaveSlot_WriteFromLive(g_SaveManager, +0xE4, +0x8C), sets the save-I/O word to 1, sets the second block to state 0 and asks the overlay to open. Phase 1 waits for the write, starts a save-index reload through the second block (resetting +0xE4 to -1), then closes the overlay and returns to state 0. Phase 2 refreshes the list and runs the row search; with +0xE4 at -1 the ordinary save branch finds no row.

Erase (agent state 7): phase 0 marks the list active, clears focus, fills the work buffer with 0xFF and copies it over the 40,164-byte cache slot, sets the save-I/O word to 1, sets the second block to state 0 and asks the overlay to open. Phase 1 waits and returns to state 0 when the block is idle; phase 2 refreshes the list.

Source pick (agent state 8; the registry lists it as UISaveLoad_StateNewGamePlus): phase 0 clears focus, calls the music helper for track 8 in mode 2, requests fade 26 and detaches the list addon. Phase 1 waits for the fade, writes +0xE4 to g_GlobalWork+128 and returns to state 0. Phase 2 runs the active test and detaches the remaining addons.

Close (agent state 9, sub_140183ED0): phase 0 marks the list active, calls the music helper for track 7 on tab 0 or track 8 on the other tabs in mode 1, requests fade 9. Phase 1 waits for the fade and returns to state 0; phase 2 clears focus and the active byte and tears the addons down.

Deferred switch (agent state 10, sub_140183FA0): reached from pause-prompt command 3 or 4, it is a wait, not a second confirmation. Phase 0 only clears focus and marks the list active. Phase 1 calls sub_1401D6DB0(qword_143CD9DD8, +0xE8, +0xEC); the pause callback sets those dwords to 13 and 1. The helper tests the UI agent in slot 13, and the state switches to +0xF0 when the helper returns 0 or when +0xE8 is still 23. The callback sets +0xF0 to 5 (command 3, load) or 8 (command 4, source pick); phase 2 clears the active byte and resets the wait pair and +0xF0.

behavior.text: the screen is one agent with eleven states; state 0 is a no-op resting state, states 1..4 bring the screen up, states 5..8 act, state 9 closes and state 10 defers a target state. The state-to-handler table is the UISaveLoadStates registry; the second block's three used states are the UISaveLoadDialogStates registry.

the mode field at +0x40 is written three ways: UISaveLoad_Open writes 2 for the load path, TitleScene_Update rewrites it to 4 for New Game +, and sub_140182DF8 writes 1 with a situation value for the save path. State 3 collects the five headers only when bit 1 is set; state 4 maps bit 0/bit 2 to the tab.

tab 0 and tab 1 both scan all 50 cache slots; tab 0 adds one entry created by sub_140186390 first, tab 1 copies the automatic vector first, and tab 2 neither copies the vector nor adds the extra entry. Tab 2 keeps only valid slots whose +0x119 byte is non-zero and whose +0x11A situation byte is 5 or 0.

the automatic vector is filled by SaveLoadList_BuildAutoEntries from the five 264-byte headers; only headers with the FFTI magic, dword 122 at +4 and a kind below 2 at +0x0C become rows. Only tab 1 copies that vector into the visible list.

the list addon is the event source. The agent forwards its events only while the list addon exists and the event source id matches; the event map stores the selection at +0xE4, the load flag at +0xF4 and the target state at +0xF0.

load and save use different completion paths: load writes g_GlobalWork+102 and +104 when it finishes, while save writes the cache slot and then reloads the save index through the second block. Erase writes 0xFF over the whole cache slot and reloads the index too.

state 10 is a wait. It sets no prompt and stores no new choice; it calls sub_1401D6DB0 for UI agent slot 13 with value 1 and then enters +0xF0 (5 for load, 8 for source pick). The initial slot value 23 skips the wait.

g_GlobalWork+128 is written only by state 8: the title seeds it with -1 and reads it after the screen closes. State 5 (load) writes g_GlobalWork+102 and +104 as flags. I: the load path therefore uses a different field, so the two callers share the screen without sharing a result field.
tab 0 is the save list, tab 1 the load list with automatic slots and tab 2 the New Game + source list (rests on the three open modes and the tab compositions; on-screen captions were not read).

the mode-1 path is the in-game save: sub_140182DF8 is called by a save helper and a blocking menu helper, sets bit 0 and stores the situation value that state 6 writes (rests on those two callers and on SaveSlot_WriteFromLive).
the on-screen labels of the tabs and prompts; which UI agent occupies slot 13 that state 10 tests; what guide 235 is; whether the dialog block's state 3 was intended.

notes: Read: the open, the ten state handlers, the event map, the pause callback, the list builders and the title's -1 seed. Three handlers have no published sheet yet (sub_1401836F0 state 2, sub_140183ED0 state 9, sub_140183FA0 state 10), so their steps point at their UISaveLoadStates entries and name the function in the text. The registry lists state 8 as UISaveLoad_StateNewGamePlus while its page is UISaveLoad_StateSourcePick. In sub_140183658, phase 1 does call sub_1400C480C as a guard. The save step's row search looks for +0xE4 after the save branch has set it to -1, so the ordinary save does not leave the cursor on a row.
open_questions: What the tabs and prompts say on screen; which UI agent occupies the state-10 wait slot 13; what guide 235 is; whether a dialog state 3 was intended; whether the save step's -1 reset is meant to clear the selection rather than place the cursor.

name: SceneTaskDispatch
summary: How the opening and title scenes advance. Scene_Init resets the scene globals and enters one of the two start scenes; one of the two scene loops then runs a single task handler per frame. The current handler is the table entry selected by the id at the top of the task stack, and handlers move the scene on by changing that stack.

members.text: Resets the scene globals, clears the task-stack depth to 0 and calls TitleScene_Start when its mode argument is non-zero, else OpeningScene_Start. The start function pushes the first id: 14 for the title scene, 0 for the opening scene.
Calls Scene_Init, then loops while bit 0 of dword_141876EE8 is set. Each pass dispatches tbl_OpeningTaskSteps[dword_1418772E0[dword_141877480 - 1]]().
Does not call Scene_Init: it seeds the same globals itself, pushes task id 9, then runs the same per-frame dispatch loop while bit 0 of dword_141876EE8 is set.

A handler advances the scene by editing the stack. TitleScene_Task (14) replaces the top id with 15, 13 or 11; OpeningScene_Resume (13) pops and re-enters OpeningScene_Start. On the next pass the loop dispatches the new top id.

behavior.text: both loops use the same table and the same stack read; the only difference at the dispatch site is the loop around it.
the id is dword_1418772E0[dword_141877480 - 1], the last id pushed. The loop does not use a handler's return value to choose the next task; it always reads the stack again.
Scene_Init does not push a task itself. It zeroes the depth and calls TitleScene_Start (mode non-zero, pushes 14) or OpeningScene_Start (mode 0, pushes 0).
SceneLoop_Run calls Scene_Init first; SceneLoop_RunAlt does not, and it starts at id 9 instead of the ids the start functions push.

the scene advances as a small stack machine: a handler either replaces the top id or pops, and the next frame reads the new top (rests on the push and pop sites read in the handlers and on the loop always reading depth - 1).

notes: Covers Scene_Init, both scene loops and the table, plus the handlers named in the steps. The first task is pushed by TitleScene_Start / OpeningScene_Start, not by Scene_Init; those two start functions are covered only around their push. TitleScene_Task and OpeningScene_Resume are mentioned as text; their own pages carry the detail.

name: TitleSceneFlow
summary: How the Enhanced title scene advances from the scene reset to a menu hand-off. `Scene_Init` or another start caller enters `TitleScene_Start`, which resets the game and party state and pushes task 14. Task 14 runs `TitleScene_Update` once per dispatch; the update shows and waits on the title menu, sends the New Game + and Load Game choices through the save/load screen, and writes a result that `TitleScene_Task` turns into task 15, task 13, task 11, or the end of the scene.

members.text: A non-zero mode calls `TitleScene_Start`; the mode-0 branch calls `OpeningScene_Start` instead. `Scene_Init` itself does not push a task.
Resets the event/legacy scene state and the game/party state, allocates the eight-byte title scene frame, shows the title menu (or seeds the save-return result 2), and pushes task id 14.
The scene loop dispatches the top id; id 14 is `TitleScene_Task`, which calls `TitleScene_Update` with the frame at `g_UIStateFade+48`.
State 1 waits until the title menu add-on is idle. State 0 re-shows the menu through `UITitle_ShowMenu`.

The chosen menu row is carried out: New Game opens the play mode screen, Continue runs inside `UIAgentFFTOTitle_Update`, Load Game and New Game + open the save/load screen, and Music Player and Select Version set their own fade/next-state values.

Load Game opens the save/load agent in mode 2; New Game + opens the same screen and then switches the agent's mode field to 4. The function only sets the save/load agent's state; it pushes no scene task.
Continue loads the newest save inside the title agent (manual-slot scan, resume header, load or resume materialiser) and ends by writing next_state 4.

When the menu or the opened screen reports idle, the update turns the title agent's next_state into a scene result: 1 -> New Game, 2 -> hand-over, 3 -> opening restart, 4 -> idle/attract restart. Load Game also checks `g_GlobalWork+102`; New Game + also checks `g_GlobalWork+128`.

Result 1 pushes task 15 (`TitleScene_NewGameHandoff`), result 2 pushes nothing and ends the scene loop, result 3 replaces task 14 with task 13 (`OpeningScene_Resume`), and result 4 pushes task 11 (`TitleScene_DemoReturn`). The scene loop dispatches the new top id next frame.
Task 13 sets scene flag bit 6, clears the page index, pops itself and re-enters `OpeningScene_Start`, which pushes task 0 and restarts the mode-0 opening.
Task 15 waits for the requested movie, pops itself, sets the page index to 1, loads opening row 1 and pushes task 1.
Task 11 waits for the demo movie, pops itself, sets the page index to 1 and scene flag 0x40, and re-enters `OpeningScene_Start`, which pushes task 0.

behavior.text: `Scene_Init` only calls `TitleScene_Start` for a non-zero mode; `TitleScene_Start` is also called by opening task 0, opening task 2, `OpeningTask_7` and `sub_14037F398`, so the title can be re-entered without `Scene_Init`.

the title scene frame is eight bytes at `g_UIStateFade+48`; +0 is the state and +1 is the result. `TitleScene_Update` reads and writes those two bytes; `TitleScene_Start` allocates the buffer, and `TitleScene_Task` calls `sub_1401DDCFC(g_UIStateFade)` at the end of every non-zero result.

state 1 of the update reads the title agent's next_state at +89: 1 = New Game confirmed on the play mode screen, 2 = New Game +, 3 = Load Game, 4 = Continue finished, 5 = Music Player, 6 = Select Version, 7 = title menu idle timeout.

New Game + and Load Game both use the save/load screen but test different fields afterwards: New Game + tests `g_GlobalWork+128` (set to -1 before the screen opens) and Load Game tests `g_GlobalWork+102` (set to 1 when a load is confirmed).
the New Game + -1 value means the screen was backed out, so the menu is shown again; any other value means a source save was chosen and the play mode screen opens (rests on the state-2 branches).

the update's navigation states 2 (play mode screen not chosen), 3 (`g_GlobalWork+102` clear) and 4 return to state 1 without a result; the result 1..4 that task 14 acts on is written by state 1 (from next_state) and by state 3 (result 2 when `g_GlobalWork+102` is non-zero). State 5 has no branch and writes nothing.

result 1 pushes task 15 after `GameState_ResetParty(0)` clears the game tables and fills one starting unit; result 2 writes the loop hand-over code `dword_141876F94` (3 for the save-return path, else 0 or 1 from event variables 85 and 100) and toggles scene flag bit 0 to end the loop; result 3 replaces the top id with 13; result 4 pushes task 11 after selecting one of NXD table-66 rows 18, 19 or 20.

task 15 (`TitleScene_NewGameHandoff`) waits for the requested movie, pops itself, sets page index 1, loads opening row 1 and pushes task 1; task 11 (`TitleScene_DemoReturn`) waits for the demo movie, pops itself, sets page index 1 and scene flag 0x40, and re-enters `OpeningScene_Start`.

the flow is menu-driven and never loads a save in the title task itself: Continue is the only path that loads inside the title agent, while Load Game and New Game + delegate to the save/load agent and come back through `g_GlobalWork` (rests on the update branches and on `UISaveLoad_Open` setting no scene task).

notes: Covers the four title-scene functions, the title agent's next_state setters, the save/load open and terminal states, and the next-task bodies 11, 13 and 15. Task 13 (`OpeningScene_Resume`), task 11 (`TitleScene_DemoReturn`) and task 15 (`TitleScene_NewGameHandoff`) are linked to their pages. Addresses are build-specific.

name: UIAgentLifecycle
summary: From the manager's construction to its teardown: the 184-byte manager is built once, fills a 54-slot agent vector, attaches addons to agents, ticks them each frame, changes their states, and finally deletes every agent and container in reverse order.

members.text: The UI manager constructor sub_1400E1D30 allocates 184 bytes, calls this constructor and stores the result at 0x143CD9DA8. The constructor sets the vtable and allocators, starts the containers empty, allocates the addon map head and calls CreateAgents.

54 agents are allocated in slot order; each is base-constructed or passed to a named constructor, given its derived vtable and appended to the vector at +16/+24/+32. The manager's init state becomes 1.
The resulting table is UIAgentSlots: one entry per slot with its id, class, vtable, constructor, allocation size and role. The vector index and the registry id are the same number.

The per-frame path pumps the manager first: sub_1401D1148 advances the init state (requesting font-slot rows from table 24 and waiting until they load) and processes the addon map, then every agent's vtable slot 1 is called in slot order, and sub_1401D144C drains the queued-event vector.
A screen addon attaches to its agent, gets an id from the manager's +0x80 counter and is inserted into the addon map at +0x30 under that id.
The old state's handler runs with 2, the new state is stored in the control block's +0x18 (agent+0x60), the selector returns the new handler, and that handler runs with 0.
The active test is the addon list: it compares the addon vector begin at +0x10 with the end at +0x18, so an agent with any addon attached reports active.

UIAgent_DetachAddon removes the addon from the agent's list, marks it closing at +0x2C and hides it. The manager's pump processes that flag and, for entries whose +0x2D byte is set, deletes the addon and erases its map node.

Teardown: the UI manager destructor calls the manager's vtable slot 0, sub_1401CF530. It releases the font slots, calls each addon's vtable slot +0x88, deletes the agents in reverse slot order, deletes the addon map values and nodes, frees all three vectors and the map, and clears 0x143CD9DA8.

behavior.text: the manager is built once, when 0x143CD9DA8 is null; the constructor is the only caller of CreateAgents, and the destructor clears the global.
the agent vector index is the slot id; the 54 slots are contiguous and their order is fixed.
the per-frame order is manager pump (font slots and addons), then every agent's vtable slot 1 in slot order, then the queued-event drain.
teardown releases the font slots first, then notifies the addons, deletes the agents in reverse slot order, deletes the addon map, frees all storage and clears the global.
addons get their id from the manager's +0x80 counter and are inserted into the map at +0x30 under that id.
the per-frame tick calls vtable slot 1 on every vector entry without a null test.
the slot order is a stable interface because screens read fixed indices (rests on the fixed-index reads at slots 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 37 and 50).
whether the manager can be rebuilt after teardown (the constructor only runs when the global is null; no second construction path was found).
what happens after an allocation left a null agent slot.

notes: Read: the two manager functions, the manager destructor and deleting destructor, the frame pump, the event drain, the addon attach and detach pages, and the existing UIAgentCursor, UIAgentFFTOTitle and UIAgentFFTOSystem pages. The flow stops at the manager boundary; addon loading and screen internals belong to ScreenAddonCreation and the screen pages. The UIAgentSlots registry, UIAgent_SetState and UIAgent_IsActive are linked from the steps.

name: UiLayerComposite
summary: One frame of UI, layer by layer, in the order the game does it: how a widget becomes layers, which target a layer's draws go to, when that target is cleared, what runs on it, and how it is blended onto the frame. Everything a software renderer needs for the Job Tree: draw each layer's pixels into a cleared layer target, then composite the layers onto the frame in order.

members.text: Start of the UI frame: 512 layer records (592 bytes) reset, layer count 0, current layer 0.
Widgets are drawn from the last entry of the widget vector to the first (the first entry is on top), each through GUICore_DrawWidget.
Builds the root draw context of the widget's main component and calls ComponentLayer_Begin with the force flag 0.

A layer is opened when the component has any enabled effect group (colour transform that is not the identity, offsets, single float, drop shadow, glow, the +186 group, the whole-layer blur group, clip, mask) or a blend type other than 0, or when the renderer feature byte (+606621, 1 from the initialiser) forces it: the widget root (widget byte +83 is 1 for every one of the 51 widgets read live) and any component with component byte +561 set. Component nodes of kind Layer (UIB 'Layer00', 'LayerRoot') are plain containers and open nothing.

Finds an existing layer record with the same layer id and equal effect settings (never when the id is 0) or builds a new one (GUILayer_BuildRecord) and makes it current; later draws are appended to the current layer.

The component's nodes are drawn last entry first; each UI draw appends its command to the current layer through UIRender_AppendCommand, which also marks the layer used (+76). A child component with effects opens its own record; when it ends GUILayer_Select(parent context) continues the parent in a NEW record with an incremented layer id, so the parent's later draws stay above the child's layer.

The used layers (list in slot order = creation order) get their order (overlap rule; the final pack order is the list sorted by the order key, see the behavior LayerAtlasPlacement) and each its rectangle in the layer atlas page (GUILayer_PackAtlasRect: the layer's integer screen rectangle plus a margin of 2 px, or 32 px when a blur radius is above 3.2); the atlas offset layer+224 / +228 = packed position - integer screen position.
For every used layer GUILayer_Composite packs the layer's commands; the commands of all contexts are then sorted by key and executed.

Clear: at the first layer of each atlas page GUILayer_Composite queues clears of the layer content target and its scratch targets (slots 26, 27, 28, 29; slot 3 when the layer has a drop shadow; slot 30 for a masked layer) to the colour (0, 0, 0, 0) (RenderCommand_ClearTarget; the 16 colour bytes of the command are zero).

Draw: the layer's own draws are replayed into the layer content target (RT 26) with the scissor rectangle = the layer's packed integer rectangle in atlas coordinates and the layer's constant buffer bound; vertices go through a pixel-to-clip matrix whose translation holds the atlas offset.

Blend of the draws: the draw state's word, 0x79420a11 by default (source ONE, destination INV_SRC_ALPHA, add, alpha the same, write mask 0xF): the layer target holds premultiplied colour; the first draw into a cleared pixel stores round8(source).

Effects of the layer in fixed order on its pixels (mask, colour / offset passes, blur, drop shadow copy and blur), skipped for a plain layer; the layer's pixels stay in RT 26 unless a pass moved them.

Blit: the layer quad (rect - atlas offset, the integer screen rectangle) is drawn with selector #9 (digit 0 = layer blend type); the pixel shader reads RT 26 at pixel + atlas offset (point read, exact texel) and does the blend by a read-modify-write of the frame target.

Blend type 0: frame = round8(layer.rgb x k + frame.rgb x (1 - layer.a)), alpha = round8(layer.a + frame.a x (1 - layer.a)), with k = cb8.z = 1 and the layer's colour transform (multiply 1, add 0 by default) applied to the layer pixels first.
Glow and shadow of the layer land after / before the blit as the existing flows describe (LayerGlowHalfSize, LayerDropShadow).

behavior.text: layers with no draws (+76 clear) are skipped by GUILayer_Composite and cost nothing; a layer with the cull flag (+79) draws and blits nothing.

all UI draws, text included, are recorded into layer records; the pass order within one atlas page is clear, then every layer's draws, then every layer's blit (key order), so the layer target never holds more than the current page.
the letterbox bars and the overlay quads (UIRender_DrawOverlayQuads) are drawn straight to the output, outside the layers.

open_questions: ? the layer ids a UIB can assign (component +552), which merge several components into one record; the kind 2 layers (never produced by GUILayer_BuildRecord).
